name: Mutton Karahi
description: Pakistani mutton karahi with tender bone-in meat and a concentrated fresh tomato masala finished with cumin, black pepper, green chillies and ginger.
ingredients: ½–1 cup hot water, only as needed
method: Heat the oil in a karahi or heavy wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the mutton and fry for several minutes, turning the pieces, until they lose their raw exterior colour and begin to brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook briefly, then add the tomatoes and salt. Cook while stirring until the tomatoes collapse and begin forming a thick masala around the meat.

Add a modest amount of hot water, cover and cook over medium-low heat until the mutton becomes tender. Check periodically and add more hot water only if the pan becomes dry before tenderness is reached.
Once the meat is tender, uncover and raise the heat moderately. Cook while stirring frequently until excess moisture evaporates and the tomato masala becomes concentrated rather than gravy-like.
Add the crushed cumin, freshly ground black pepper and green chillies near the end so their aroma remains distinct. Cook a few more minutes until the masala clings well to the mutton.
Taste for salt, garnish generously with julienned fresh ginger and serve hot with naan or roti.
tips: Mutton may need longer than 70 minutes depending on the cut and age of the meat; tenderness is more important than a fixed clock time.
Avoid adding a large amount of water at once because karahi should finish with a concentrated tomato masala rather than a thin gravy.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate covered. Reheat the portion being served until thoroughly hot.
image_alt: Pakistani mutton karahi with tender bone-in meat, concentrated fresh tomato masala, green chilli and ginger
image_caption: Mutton cooked tender first, then finished uncovered until fresh tomato masala clings to the meat.
technique: Tenderness comes before final karahi reduction. Use a modest amount of hot water only as needed to soften the mutton, then uncover and reduce the tomatoes aggressively enough to concentrate without drying the meat.
doneness_cues: Mutton should yield easily before the final high-moisture reduction ends.
Tomatoes should break down completely into a clinging masala.
No large pool of thin gravy should remain.
Fresh ginger, cumin, pepper and green chilli should remain distinct at the finish.
mistakes: Trying to keep karahi dry from the beginning and leaving mutton tough.
Adding a large quantity of water and ending with curry-like gravy.
Continuing reduction long after meat is tender and drying it out.
Adding finishing spices too early so their aroma disappears.
substitutions: Mutton cuts vary greatly; use tenderness rather than minutes as the endpoint.
Reduce green chilli without reducing fresh ginger.
If tomatoes are watery, use a wider pan rather than flour.
reheating: Reheat gently with a spoonful of water only if needed.
serving: Serve with naan or roti and extra julienned ginger.
